summary.text: Wayne Woodfield is the Utah Forward Party candidate for the Utah State Senate, District 21, in the November 3, 2026 general election, challenging Republican incumbent Brady Brammer.
A software engineer, he said in a Ballotpedia survey that he is running to restore integrity, civility, unity and fair governance to the legislature.

paragraphs.text: Woodfield graduated from Springville High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Brigham Young University in 2002, according to his Ballotpedia profile.
The profile lists his career experience as working as a software engineer.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he was born in Provo, raised in Mapleton and currently lives in Lehi.
Woodfield said in the survey that he was a precinct chair in the Republican Party about 10 years ago.

He described his approach as taking ideas from across the political spectrum, and said he supports vote-by-mail and independent processes for redistricting and ballot language for constitutional amendments.
He named education, affordable housing and water management as high priorities, and said he favors reasonable term limits, campaign finance reform and stronger checks and balances.
